Interesting that the binary from the python packages and the from source build are differing here.

You can set `-iree-llvm-target-triple` to target any machine (from the LLVM targets that have been compiled in / initialized, see the bottom of [LLVMAOTTarget.cpp](https://github.com/google/iree/blob/aae314e8bb72115aa00ce2556fbd8ed1559d459d/iree/compiler/Dialect/HAL/Target/LLVM/LLVMAOTTarget.cpp)): https://github.com/google/iree/blob/aae314e8bb72115aa00ce2556fbd8ed1559d459d/iree/compiler/Dialect/HAL/Target/LLVM/LLVMTargetOptions.cpp#L66-L68 (also see the other options in that file)

For example, I've set `-iree-llvm-target-triple=x86_64-linux-gnu` to compile for Linux from Windows.

If you don't set those options explicitly, they'll default to what LLVM can infer: https://github.com/google/iree/blob/aae314e8bb72115aa00ce2556fbd8ed1559d459d/iree/compiler/Dialect/HAL/Target/LLVM/LLVMTargetOptions.cpp#L28-L30

Thanks @ScottTodd! setting `-iree-llvm-target-triple=arm64-apple-darwin21.4.0` got it working! 

```
Interesting that the binary from the python packages and the from source build are differing here.
```
It is peculiar that source built infer Arm, and prebuilt infer X86 😅 .  Perhaps `llvm::sys::getDefaultTargetTriple()` automatically load the clang it was built on's defaults?
@stellaraccident fyi since she has her M1 now.

> It is peculiar that source built infer Arm, and prebuilt infer X86  . Perhaps `llvm::sys::getDefaultTargetTriple()` automatically load the clang it was built on's defaults?

I am guessing that is exactly what it is doing.

llvm::sys::getDefaultTargetTriple() `returns the default target triple the compiler has been configured to produce code for` and in particular it is set at the point where iree-compile is compiled (so for universal binary I'm assuming that during compilation time it only gets set for x86 and that same config used both sides). We could potentially use `getProcessTriple` instead which should give the triple of the machine being run on [I was trying to verify that but kept running into other issues today].
AFAIK this has been fixed in [abc3ac999ea3a2cdea9fdb920dbf368e708eeef7](https://github.com/openxla/iree/commit/abc3ac999ea3a2cdea9fdb920dbf368e708eeef7).
Looks like it. Please re-open if there are still issues.

issue.body: ### Problem: Trying to run e2e Resnet model on M1 with preinstalled binaries but ran into device not supported. ```bash RuntimeError: Error invoking function: :0: UNKNOWN; device not supported in the compiled configuration; [ 0] bytecode module.forward:1996 :279:10 ``` #### Further investigation show that issue stem from iree-compile ```bash /Users/user/venv/shark/lib/python3.9/site-packages/iree/compiler/_mlir_libs/iree-compile --iree-mlir-to-vm-bytecode-module -iree-hal-target-backends=dylib /tmp/Resnet50Module.mlir -iree-vm-bytecode-source-listing=foo.mlir -o Resnet50Module-dylib.vmfb iree-build/iree/tools/iree-benchmark-module --driver=dylib --entry_function=forward --function_input=1x3x224x224xf32 --module_file=Resnet50Module-dylib.vmfb --benchmark_repetitions=1 # Result: Running ../iree-build/iree/tools/iree-benchmark-module Run on (8 X 24.2407 MHz CPU s) CPU Caches: L1 Data 64 KiB (x8) L1 Instruction 128 KiB (x8) L2 Unified 4096 KiB (x2) Load Average: 1.58, 1.52, 1.51 :0: UNKNOWN; device not supported in the compiled configuration; [ 0] bytecode module.forward:1996 [ /tmp/Resnet50Module.mlir:279:10 at /tmp/Resnet50Module.mlir:9:3, "vm"(foo.mlir:295:4) ] [1] 84694 abort ../iree-build/iree/tools/iree-benchmark-module --driver=vulkan ``` But when I use iree-compile built from source it can translate and run fine. Looking at the iree-vm-bytecode-source-listing seems like the **preinstalled binary iree-compile** is generating **x86**: While if we run **iree-compile built from source** it will generate **ARM**: I was wondering if there is a way to set the iree-compile to generate ARM instead of x86?
